parts:
Hi!

That error indicates that some function crashed during calculation of the likelihood.  check_BioGeoBEARS_run() doesn't check every imaginable thing, so most likely explanation is that something was left out of the inputs, or a filename was input that doesn't correspond to the exact location and path of the actual file.  So, make sure each of the several bits of code in the example script related to stratification are un-commented, and the files exist exactly where you told BioGeoBEARS_run_object they are, then re-run from the top line-by-line.  Have you gotten the stratified calculations to work on the default Psychotria dataset?

Cheers,
Nick

OK, so you're doing a stratified analysis.  So, more questions:

1. Did you get the default example unstratified analysis to run?  If #2 doesn't fix it right away, go back and focus on getting the unstratified analysis to work.

2. Either way, sometimes stratified analyses in particular crash if some tiny tiny probability calculation causes an underflow error.  This seems to be unpredictable and machine-dependent, but, typically the way to fix this, which has worked for many people, is to change the zeros in the dispersal matrix to e.g. 0.00001.  So, try that.

3. Looks like you have optimx 2012, you might as well update to optimx 2013, as that now works with BioGeoBEARS.

4. I can't double check that your input paths and filenames are correct, but these all have to be exactly right, sometimes people accidentally rename the geography file or whatever.

Cheers, Nick

Hiya!

OK, so you're doing a stratified analysis.  So, more questions:

1. Did you get the default example unstratified analysis to run?  If #2 doesn't fix it right away, go back and focus on getting the unstratified analysis to work.

2. Either way, sometimes stratified analyses in particular crash if some tiny tiny probability calculation causes an underflow error.  This seems to be unpredictable and machine-dependent, but, typically the way to fix this, which has worked for many people, is to change the zeros in the dispersal matrix to e.g. 0.00001.  So, try that.

3. Looks like you have optimx 2012, you might as well update to optimx 2013, as that now works with BioGeoBEARS.

4. I can't double check that your input paths and filenames are correct, but these all have to be exactly right, sometimes people accidentally rename the geography file or whatever.

Cheers, Nick
